newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to launch road project with share issue.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to launch road project with share issue.

text.p: Croatia will launch a key road building project in the tourist region of Istria this week with a 12.45 million kuna share issue, representatives of the concessionaire Bina Istra said on Thursday.
The issuer is Istarska Autocesta d.d., the smallest of three shareholders in Bina Istra, its consultant Branko Tencic told Reuters by telephone.
French firm Bouygues and Bina Finkom, in which Croatia's national oil firm INA Industrija Nafte a stake, control 83 percent of the company.
Daily Slobodna Dalmacija said works would begin in April or spring. No Bina Istra officials were available to comment.

The project to build a modern Y-shaped road network through the Istrian peninsula, close to neighbouring Slovenia and Italy, has been described by state and regional officials as potentially "very lucrative".
It is part of Croatia's plans to build a modern 40 billion kuna ($8.5 billion) road infrastructure with links to main European corridors by year 2005.

"This is the most interesting investment in Croatia through which international capital will enable an economic, and particularly tourist recovery of the region and the country," head of the Istrian Chamber of Commerce, Sime Vidulin, was quoted as saying by Slobodna Dalmacija.
Most funds are hoped to be raised through foreign credits and the concessionaire capital, the newspaper said.
The Istrian project is planned in two stages. At first, over 100 km of semi-motorway will be built and then expanded to make the Y-road into a proper motorway.
To finance it, three main shareholders have to provide 75 million German marks over the next four years, said Tencic.
He said Istarska Autocesta share issue would open on February 21, but would be subject to pre-emptive rights of the issuer's own shareholders for 60 days.
It is aimed to draw to the project both Croatian and foreign investors, corporate and retail investors alike.
The issue will be divided into 41,500 shares with a 300-kuna face value.
"The interest is difficult to assess but we can only hope that demand will be stronger than the amount of shares on offer," Tencic added.
